newsitem.title: USA: Phone group charges SBC application fraudulent.
newsitem.headline: Phone group charges SBC application fraudulent.

text.p: A phone industry trade group will ask federal regulators Wednesday to reject SBC Communications Inc's bid to provide long-distance service, charging that the Baby Bell knowingly included errors in its application.
"We're charging they made fraudulent claims in their petition," Jim Crawford, a spokesman for the Association for Local Telecommunications Services, said Tuesday.
ALTS represents about 33 carriers that provide local phone service in competition with the Bells and other local phone monopolies.

Crawford declined to go into details about the group's upcoming petition to the Federal Communications Commission, noting that ALTS will hold a press briefing on Wednesday. An SBC spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
Crawford said the alleged inaccuracies in SBC's application were "a bit more serious" than the errors that led Ameritech Corp to pull its own long-distance application earlier this year.
ALTS had challenged the Ameritech bid but did not argue that the Chicago-based carrier's application was fraudulent.
SBC received a setback last week in its bid to be the first Baby Bell to enter the $80 billion long-distance business, in Oklahoma.

A state administrative law judge there told the Oklahoma Corporation Commission that the San Antonio, Texas-based parent of Southwestern Bell had not met a federal checklist showing the carrier had opened its local phone network to competitors.
